title: Officer cleared in fatal shooting of Calgary man wielding 'Walther PPK' pellet pistol
subtitle: Investigation determines 'the officer involved was faced with what appeared to be an immediate lethal threat'
article: The Calgary police officer who killed a man wielding a pellet gun that resembles a genuine firearm was justified in the decision to shoot, the province's law enforcement review agency has determined.

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) announced Thursday that the officer had been cleared in the Oct. 31, 2014 incident, in which a 30-year-old man was shot dead at a downtown affordable housing complex for single men.

"When the man pointed what appeared to be a handgun at police, the officer involved was faced with what appeared to be an immediate lethal threat and there were objectively reasonable grounds to believe that the use of lethal force was required to prevent imminent death or grievous bodily harm to both himself and the other officers on scene," ASIRT said in a release.
Officers responded to the housing complex at 433 Macleod Trail S.E. shortly after 2 a.m. after receiving a 911 call about a man with a gun who had been making threats.

According to the ASIRT report, four officers set up containment points around the apartment suite where the man was located, two of them armed with C8 carbine rifles, one armed with a shotgun and one with a service pistol.
The layout of the building "provided only limited cover for police officers," the report noted.

Police tried to contact the man by telephone unsuccessfully and then, after being advised there were grounds for arrest, the four officers approached the suite door in formation, knocked on the door, and then retreated to the limited cover of an alcove in the apartment's hallway.

"Almost immediately, a 30-year-old man exited the suite carrying what appeared to be a handgun in his right hand, holding it flat against his chest with the gun barrel pointed to his left, away from the officers," the report states. "The man stood just outside the doorway of the suite facing the hallway, with the officers in an alcove to the man's right."
One of the officers yelled "gun" and the man turned to his right, angling the barrel of the gun towards the officers.

The nearest officer, who was about four metres away, then fired his C8 rifle twice, with one shot hitting the man in his left torso, and the second shot missing, striking the wall to the side of the suite door.
The man retreated into the suite, partially closing the door. Police yelled at him to come out but he did not respond.
The four officers waited until a tactical team arrived and sent a robot into the suite with a camera, which found the man lying dead inside.
The handgun the man had been holding was found beside his body. It turned out to be a a Crosman "Walther PPK" CO2-powered pellet pistol.
The pellet gun was "manufactured to resemble a Walther PPK semi-automatic pistol," the report noted.
An autopsy confirmed the man died from a single gunshot wound to his left torso and was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the confrontation.
"This finding in no way diminishes the sad fact that a family has lost a loved one," ASIRT said in a release.
"On behalf of ASIRT, the executive director extends condolences to the man's family and friends."
